01 What we do

The money is already in the building.

When you buy, build or refurbish a commercial healthcare property, a large share of what you spend goes into things the tax system treats as plant, machinery and fixtures — the heating and ventilation, the wiring and lighting, the lifts, the clinical and care-specific equipment built into the fabric.

Those items carry capital allowances: a long-standing, statutory relief against your income or corporation tax. Yet most owners never claim the bulk of them, because spotting the embedded fixtures takes a specialist surveyor — not a routine accounts exercise.

We identify what qualifies, value it properly, and turn it into a claim you can file. Our fee is 3% of the capital allowances we identify, stated in pounds before you commit.

20–45%of a healthcare property's value can qualify as plant and fixtures
100%relief available in year one on qualifying spend, in many cases
02 How it works

Four steps, led by people.

No black boxes. A surveyor's inspection, a documented apportionment, and a report your accountant or tax adviser signs from.

i.

A free entitlement assessment

Tell us about your property and we'll give you an honest, deliberately conservative estimate of what may be claimable — with no obligation.

ii.

A surveyor visits

A surveyor inspects the building and identifies every qualifying fixture, fitting and embedded service.

iii.

We prepare the claim report

We produce a fully documented report and apportionment, and work alongside your accountant, who signs the filing position — we don't. If you don't have one, you remain responsible for it.

iv.

You receive your relief

Your claim reduces the tax you owe. Most claims lower future bills rather than producing money back — but if your return for the purchase year is still open, part of it can also come back as a repayment for that year. We confirm which applies before anything is filed.

03 Sectors we work in

Healthcare property is where the value hides.

These buildings are unusually dense with qualifying plant and fixtures — which is exactly why so much goes unclaimed.

Care homes
Fixture-rich throughout — assisted bathing, nurse-call, passenger lifts, commercial kitchens, laundries and heating. Among the strongest claims we see.
Assessed, not independently calibrated
Dental
Surgeries are packed with embedded services — compressed air, suction ring mains, decontamination rooms and imaging. Much of it is never claimed.
Assessed, not independently calibrated
GP & primary care
Consulting and treatment suites and the building's services qualify — with care taken around NHS premises funding, which we handle for you.
Assessed, not independently calibrated
Private hospitals
The richest of all — operating theatres, medical gas, imaging and sterile services carry substantial, high-value relief.
Assessed, not independently calibrated
Supported living
Handled honestly. The claim is usually limited to communal and staff areas — and if there's little to recover, we'll tell you straight.
Honest by default

06 Pricing

One percentage, and we tell you what it's a percentage of.

Our fee is 3% of the capital allowances we identify, not 3% of the tax you save. Those are very different numbers, so here is the difference in pounds before you sign anything.

How the fee is worked out

3% of the capital allowances we identify — stated in pounds before you commit

If the survey identifies £200,000 of capital allowances, our fee is £6,000. We set out the allowances figure, and the fee it gives, in pounds in your engagement letter before any paid work starts. The rate is the same whether you have one property or several. There is no minimum fee and no minimum job size.

Not 3% of the tax you save

The base makes a fourfold difference

On £500,000 of capital allowances our fee is £15,000. If it were 3% of the tax saved at a 25% rate, it would be £3,750. That is why we never show the percentage without saying what it is a percentage of.

Read this before you sign

The fee is not capped by what you save in tax this year

Capital allowances are usually claimed gradually, as writing-down allowances on a reducing balance at the rate in force for each period, sometimes over close to a decade, while our fee falls due at once, once the claim is agreed. So the tax you actually save in any single year can be, and often is, less than the fee itself. The fee is not capped by, and may exceed, the tax you save in year one. Your engagement letter sets out your own figures: the allowances identified, the fee that follows from them, and an illustration of how the tax saving unwinds over time. If any of that isn't clear, ask us; if you're unhappy with how it was explained, our complaints procedure covers exactly this.

If the figure goes down, so does the fee

A term of the engagement letter, not a goodwill gesture

Our fee is a stated share of a stated figure. If the capital allowances identified are later reduced (after an HMRC enquiry, a correction by us, or a revision by your accountant or tax adviser), we recalculate the fee on the corrected figure and credit the difference, or refund it if you have already paid, on the terms your engagement letter sets out. For example, if the allowances fall from £73,740 to £50,000, a 3% fee falls from £2,212.20 to £1,500, and £712.20 comes back to you.

What the fee pays for, and what it doesn't

We identify and value the capital allowances and give you a report that shows the working. We don't decide what goes on your tax return and we don't sign the filing position: your accountant or tax adviser does. If you don't have one, you remain responsible for the filing position, and our report is an input to it.

Methodology & sign-off chain

The short version of what happens between an entitlement estimate and a number your client can file: a survey, an apportionment and a report from us, and a filing position signed by you.

i.
Survey

A surveyor inspects the property and identifies every qualifying embedded fixture, not a desktop guess.

ii.
Apportionment

Qualifying spend is apportioned against the purchase price on a just-and-reasonable basis under CAA 2001 s.562, referenced to the survey.

iii.
Report to you

A documented report sets out the figures, the assumptions and the caveats (entitlement, pooling history, election and notification requirements), ready for your review.

iv.
You sign the filing position

You decide what goes on the client's return and sign it. We don't. Where a client has no adviser of their own, the client remains responsible for the filing position and our report is an input to it.

Every online estimate a client sees before that point is explicitly labelled a pre-diligence ceiling — the most the sector band allows before any of this has happened — never a valuation and never advice. It can only move down from there, never up.

Is there unclaimed tax relief in your building?

If your business owns the freehold or long leasehold of a healthcare property — a care home, dental or GP practice, private hospital or supported living scheme — there may be tax relief on items inside it that has never been claimed. This isn't about what you spend from now on; it's about fixtures already built into the building: heating, lifts, catering, medical gas, nurse-call and similar embedded services.

  • A specialist survey identifies what qualifies — not a guess from a spreadsheet.
  • We identify and value the allowances; your accountant or tax adviser signs the filing position. If you have neither, you are responsible for it.
  • Our fee is 3% of the capital allowances we identify, not of the tax you save, and it can be more than the tax you save in the first year. If a proper look finds nothing worth claiming, you're told early, in writing.

This is not tax advice and no figure here is a guarantee. Capital allowances are a form of income or corporation tax relief on qualifying property expenditure — separate from capital gains tax. Ask your accountant, or start a free entitlement estimate.

08 Questions, answered

The honest answers.

Sounds too good to be true — is it legitimate?

Entirely. Capital allowances are a statutory tax relief set out in the Capital Allowances Act 2001 — the government's own way of letting businesses write down what they spend on qualifying property. We don't create anything; we identify the relief you're already entitled to and document it properly.

Will a claim trigger an HMRC enquiry?

Ours are prepared to the standard of evidence HMRC expects: a surveyor's inspection and a just-and-reasonable apportionment, with the filing position signed by your own accountant or tax adviser, or by you if you have neither. No one can promise how HMRC will respond to a particular claim.

My accountant handles my tax — won't they have claimed this?

Usually only in part. Accountants reliably claim the obvious, loose items; the embedded fixtures — the services built into the fabric of the building — need a specialist surveyor to identify and value. We work alongside your accountant, not instead of them, and hand them a filing-ready report. If you'd rather send your accountant straight to us, that's exactly what our accountant page is for.

What does it cost?

Our fee is 3% of the capital allowances we identify, not 3% of the tax you save, stated in pounds in your engagement letter before any paid work starts. It is not capped by, and may be more than, the tax you save in the first year. If the allowances are later reduced, we recalculate the fee on the corrected figure and credit or refund the difference, on the terms in your engagement letter. See how pricing works for the full detail.

Is this the same as capital gains tax?

No — and it's a common mix-up. Capital allowances are a relief against your income or corporation tax, based on what you've spent on qualifying items in your property. They're separate from capital gains tax entirely.

Do you cover Scotland and Northern Ireland?

Not yet. The assessment on this site is currently set up for England and Wales. Capital allowances are a UK-wide tax, so the relief itself is just as available in Scotland and Northern Ireland — but the property and regulatory registers this tool reads from to fill your answers in are held by different bodies there. HM Land Registry, for instance, covers England and Wales only; Scotland has Registers of Scotland and Northern Ireland has Land Registry NI. Rather than put a number in front of you built on sources we haven’t verified, we say so. If your property is in Scotland or Northern Ireland, get in touch and we’ll handle the claim the manual way — the same survey, apportionment and report for your own accountant or tax adviser, without the automated pre-diligence step.

How long does it take?

From survey to a filing-ready report is typically a few weeks, depending on the property and how quickly documents come together. The initial entitlement estimate takes minutes.
